symptom: On MPR v2 every catalog refresh opened every .mxunit (4,753 on a large app) after every save; Windows users measured the virus scanner's per-open cost as the bulk of their wait (77% faster with the project excluded from scanning)
cause: The reader's only persistent knowledge of a unit was its type and name (the unit index); its bytes were always re-read from the unit's own file, and a refresh needs every unit's bytes
file: `modelsdk/mpr/reader_unit_store.go` (`unitStore`: lookup / record / flush), `modelsdk/mpr/reader_units.go` (`readMprContents`, `buildUnitCache` row hashes, flush on the outermost `CacheUnitReads` release), `modelsdk/mpr/reader.go` (`Close`)
insight: **On Windows the cost is the open, not the bytes, so cache the bytes behind a check that does not open the file.** A stat (size + modification time, taken BEFORE the read so a file caught mid-write is stored under the old stat) plus the Unit row's ContentsHash decides a hit; the hash alone is not enough because a plain git checkout can leave it stale, and the stat alone misses a copy with preserved timestamps. Each safeguard has its own test and each test fails with its safeguard removed — the first stat control passed anyway because the changed name had another length and the post-decode size check caught it, and the first hash control 'passed' because stubbing it left a variable unused and the package did not compile: grep for `--- FAIL` and `FAIL` lines and a compile error, not only the former. The store sits in `.mxcli/cache/` with its own `.gitignore` because `.mxcli/` is not ignored in every project
fix: Persist zstd-compressed unit bytes in `.mxcli/cache/unit-contents.db`, serve a unit from it while size, mtime and row hash match, record misses and flush at the end of a full pass and on Close, drop units the Unit table no longer has. Tests: `TestUnitStore_*` (modelsdk/mpr) and `TestCatalogRefresh_NextProcessOpensOnlyChangedUnits` (executor: 369 files → 0, 1 after one file changes, catalog row-identical to a build that read every file)
